name: On the Record
tagline: You don't like being the only one. You like pretending even less.

sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/joseph-james-forrester.md`. *Dictionary of National Biography* vol. 20 (1889), pp. 14–15, entry by Ellen Mary Clerke, read in full on Wikisource (secondary, period, signed). *The Oxford Companion to Spirits and Cocktails*, ELDER (pdf 707, primary). *The Cocktail Codex* (port, p. 250; the Bamboo shape, p. 91; p. 9). *The Flavor Matrix*, Cocoa and Fig charts (pdf 85, 121; port, red wine and tea in the Phenol group). Web (Hester's 2 visits): Wikisource (DNB) and one archive.org full-text search (`"Forrester" "import duties on wines"`), OCR highlights only, each labelled as cut off (Barr, *Drink*; *Edinburgh Review* 1867; Simpson, *Creating Wine*, 2011).
names_note: Vote in round 4, steps 3–4: *On the Record* 2–1 (Tomás, Hester); Wren voted *The Second Time* and recorded the room's pick in her title block. Also considered: *Said Twice*, *Still There*, *At Greater Length*. Picks were held until the vote.
open_items: FLAGGED, balance by choice: balance.py (`stirred`) reads strength (10.8% finished vs 21–29), acid (0.27% vs 0.10–0.14) and dilution (29.6% vs 41–49) OUT. Tomás keeps the wine core by choice and justifies it in Checks: a port core can't reach a spirit Martini's strength, and wine carries its own acid (the Codex's Bamboo shape; sibling *Night Light* reads the same way).

Port residual sugar has no source in the library: across 8.5–13 g/100 ml the finished sugar runs 4.99–7.08 g/100 ml, EDGE at mid-range values and OUT for the sweetest bottles. Library gap named by Hester: Mayson, *Port and the Douro* (2012).

Whether Forrester was right is contested (card C3): the reading never says he was. He shipped port and was not a disinterested party in the 1852 duties debate (C4); Hester struck her own r2 line that merged two cut-off fragments.

Hester's step-4 edge: y4's "as a nod to his second telling" counts the tellings, but the reading gives three (1844, 1845, 1852). If Robin wants the count exact, her fix is "as a nod to his second telling" → "as a nod to his telling it again" (not applied; the room had signed).

Unread leads on the card: the 1852 *Report* itself (his answers from q. 36), and the end of Barr's "written off" sentence (*Drink*, p. 84). Offley as a port brand today is unverified, so no bottle is named.
The colour in the image brief is Tomás's estimate.
